item.title: Gombe approves N97bn road projects, N3.8bn emergency vehicles
item.description: …SEC endorses 2027–2029 expenditure framework, updates social protection policy .. Government targets December resumption of Kolmani oil exploration By Ben Ngwakwe, Gombe GOMBE — The Gombe State Executive Council (SEC), presided over by Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya, has approved seven road projects valued at billions of naira, covering approximately 97 kilometres across four local government areas of the state. The council also approved the procurement of 40 emergency response and public utility vehicles, comprising 20 firefighting trucks and 20 water tankers, at a combined cost of about N3.8 billion. Other major decisions taken at the council meeting on Monday included the approval of the 2027–2029 Medium-Term Expenditure Framework (MTEF), an updated Social Protection Policy for 2027–2030 and measures to position the state to benefit from the anticipated resumption of oil exploration in the Kolmani area in December. Briefing journalists after the meeting, the Commissioner for Information and Culture, Moses Kyari Bolda, said the decisions reflected the administration’s commitment to infrastructure development, improved public services and long-term economic growth. On the road projects, the Commissioner for Works and Infrastructure, Shehu Yarima Abdullahi, said the council approved seven memoranda presented by his ministry for projects covering Yamaltu-Deba, Balanga, Shongom and Kaltungo Local Government Areas. Among the approved projects is the 18.9-kilometre Talasse-Bangu-Boka Bundi-Walalunguda Road, including a spur to Dalawaja, awarded to Datum Construction Company Limited at N23.98 billion, with a completion period of 24 months. Similarly, the 38-kilometre Lapan-Labariya-Lasanjan-Latatar-Lakunturum Road, with a spur to Burak, was awarded to EEC International Limited at N49.3 billion, also with a 24-month completion period. The council also approved the first phase of the Bangunji-Dadiya-Yelwa-Gombe/Yola Road project, covering approximately 15 kilometres, to be executed by EEC International Limited at N26.3 billion. Other projects include the initial four-kilometre section of the Degri-Sikam-Nyuwar Kindiyo Road, covering Degri to Sikam, awarded to Datum Construction Company Limited at approximately N4 billion. The 10.5-kilometre Dogon Ruwa-Kaltin Road was also awarded to the company at about N10.1 billion, while the nine-kilometre Kurjale-Pata Road was awarded to EEC International Limited. The seventh project, covering 1.5 kilometres of the Kunuwal Road Network, was awarded to Swas Grade Limited. Abdullahi explained that the Degri-Sikam-Nyuwar Kindiyo Road would be implemented in phases, with the initial four-kilometre stretch from Degri to Sikam approved as the first phase. item.title: Mimiko congratulates Aiyedatiwa on Silverbird award
item.description: …Urges Ondo governor to deepen dividends of democracy By Dayo Johnson, Akure Former Governor of Ondo State, Dr Olusegun Mimiko, has congratulated Governor Lucky Orimisan Aiyedatiwa on emerging as the 2026 Silverbird Governor of the Year. Mimiko described the award as recognition of the achievements recorded so far by the Aiyedatiwa administration and its efforts towards developing the state. The award was presented at the 20th edition of the Silverbird Man of the Year Awards held at Eko Hotels, Lagos. In a congratulatory message, the former governor urged Aiyedatiwa to see the recognition as a call to do more for the people of Ondo State and deepen the dividends of democracy. He said the honour by the Silverbird Group showed that the governor’s efforts were receiving recognition beyond the state. “This honour from the Silverbird Group is an acknowledgement that your efforts are being noticed and should, therefore, spur you to do more for the benefit of the greater majority of our compatriots in our dear state,” Mimiko said. He described Ondo State’s selection for the award among the 36 states as encouraging, noting that it reflected efforts being made across different sectors and communities. “It is encouraging to see Ondo State singled out among the 36 states for this award. It speaks to some work being done across sectors and locations in the state,” he added. Mimiko prayed for greater strength and wisdom for Aiyedatiwa as he continues to steer the affairs of the state. item.title: Anambra Patriots endorse APGA-APC alliance, adopt Tinubu for 2027
item.description: By Chimaobi Nwaiwu NNEWI — A political pressure group in Anambra State, Anambra Patriots, APS, has endorsed the alliance between the All Progressives Grand Alliance, APGA, and the All Progressives Congress, APC, adopting President Bola Tinubu as its preferred candidate for the 2027 presidential election. The group also declared its support for the re-election of Anambra State Governor, Professor Chukwuma Soludo, and urged Ndigbo to support his political direction, including his backing for Tinubu. The convener of APS and Anambra State Commissioner for Works, Architect Okey Ezeobi, disclosed the group’s position on Sunday during the Anambra Patriots Women Summit held in Awka, the state capital. Ezeobi expressed dissatisfaction with those criticising Soludo for aligning politically with Tinubu rather than supporting former Anambra State governor and Labour Party presidential candidate in the 2023 election, Peter Obi. He argued that politics should be driven by interests rather than sentiments, insisting that Soludo’s decision to support Tinubu was in the interest of Ndigbo. “My problem with Ndigbo is that they don’t know how to play politics. We do politics of emotion instead of interest. In politics, you get what you contributed, not what you deserve. Politics is about interest,” he said. According to him, Soludo’s support for Tinubu was not motivated by personal gains but by what he described as the need for greater political inclusion of the South-East in national affairs. He said: “Prof. Soludo’s support for Tinubu is not for personal gain, but for the interest of Ndigbo. It is time for Ndigbo to come back to Nigeria. And Soludo is a professor; he has analysed Nigerian politics.” Ezeobi also argued that Soludo should not be criticised for his political choice, saying other ethnic groups had members supporting Obi without attracting similar criticism. He urged Anambra residents to recognise Soludo’s position as governor and support his political decisions, adding that backing Obi was not compulsory for every Igbo politician. “Why is everybody seeing Soludo as an enemy because he is supporting Tinubu? If we accept Soludo as our leader and governor in Anambra State, we must follow him anywhere he is pitching his political tent. It is not compulsory that we must support Peter Obi. Politics is not about sentiments,” he said. The commissioner also made several claims about the political relationship between Obi and Soludo, alleging that Obi had opposed Soludo’s governorship ambition on previous occasions. He cited the 2013, 2021 and 2025 governorship election cycles in Anambra, claiming that Obi had supported different political moves against Soludo, which ultimately failed. Ezeobi, however, maintained that Soludo had not insulted Obi but had only responded to comments he considered critical of Anambra State and APGA. item.title: True fulfilment lies in impacting lives, says Ooni
item.description: … Backs YASA Foundation’s drive for inclusive society By Ogochukwu Agha lagos—The Ooni of Ife, Oba Adeyeye Ogunwusi, has urged Nigerians, corporate organisations and philanthropists to support initiatives that empower vulnerable people, saying true fulfilment lies in making positive impact on others. The monarch spoke at the unveiling of the Yeye Afolashade Shona-Aluko (YASA) Foundation in Lagos, where he donated N5 million. Describing the foundation’s humanitarian mission as worthy of support, Oba Ogunwusi said: “What gives the greatest happiness in this world is a life of impact and fulfilment. Everybody is chasing money. But when you attain a certain level of wealth, you discover that money does not necessarily bring happiness. “The essence of life is what you can give to others.” Senator Sylvia Mthethwa of Eswatini urged governments and institutions to promote inclusive development, asking: “Are we developing societies in which everybody has an opportunity to participate or contribute and prosper?” She called for improved access to education, healthcare and employment for persons with disabilities. The Ooni’s wife, Olori Temitope Enitan-Ogunwusi, commended the foundation’s founder, urging her to remain committed to humanitarian service despite challenges. Earlier, Shona-Aluko said her youngest son’s disability inspired her intervention. She recalled employing eight specialised teachers to support him and other children at Ikeja High School for about nine years. She said the experience exposed the difficulties faced by families unable to afford specialised education. “YASA Foundation was born from a burden… a burden to give voice to the voiceless, strength to the weak, and to say boldly: ‘You are not forgotten,’” she said. The foundation focuses on inclusive education, healthcare, rehabilitation, assistive devices, vocational training and livelihood support. The event featured beneficiaries’ testimonies and recognition of Shona-Aluko by two international institutions. The post True fulfilment lies in impacting lives, says Ooni appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Expert pushes unified emergency response system to save lives
item.description: By Sola Ogundipe Nigeria needs a unified emergency response system that connects patients to ambulances, appropriately equipped hospitals, medical specialists and health insurance providers through a single call, an emergency care expert and healthcare entrepreneur has stated. Giving the warning in Lagos,during the inaugural ResQ Summit 2026, Dr. Aisha Onisarotu Atanda, who is the Chief Executive Officer of The Ambulance Company, ResQCore and TAC Care, said that the absence of such coordination continues to expose patients to avoidable delays and risks. Atanda, who convened the Summit themed “Building a Coordinated Emergency System”, said an integrated emergency care network would eliminate the burden on patients and their relatives to independently arrange transportation, identify suitable hospitals, secure specialist intervention and negotiate access to treatment during life-threatening situations. Speaking at the Rescue Summit 2026, themed “Building a Coordinated Emergency Care System”, Atanda said Nigeria already had organisations and resources providing different aspects of emergency care, but poor coordination prevented them from functioning as one effective system. She said the current arrangement often left families struggling to determine which emergency number to call, secure an ambulance and identify a hospital capable of managing the patient’s condition, resulting in delays that could compromise survival. “The problem we have at the moment is that many organisations operate in silos. Hospitals operate independently. Ambulance companies and health maintenance organisations are also doing their own thing, all with the right intention of improving emergency care. “However, when these organisations operate in silos, patients and their relatives are left to navigate the system themselves. They have to figure out which number to call, contact an ambulance and then decide where the patient should be taken,” Atanda said. She noted that the proposed model would ensure that once an emergency call was received, the patient’s location and condition would be established, an appropriate ambulance dispatched and a receiving hospital with the capacity to provide the required treatment identified. Atanda said the initiative is particularly important in emergencies involving burns, complicated pregnancies and other conditions requiring specialised intervention, where taking a patient to the wrong facility could result in dangerous delays. “The patient’s relatives may not have the expertise to know, for instance, that a burn victim needs to be taken to a specialist burns centre. As a result, valuable time is wasted accessing the wrong care when the patient could have been connected to the right facility through a coordinated system,” she added. item.title: 67th NCH: Nasarawa seeks actionable resolutions to improve healthcare delivery
item.description: By Chidinma Chukwu, Abuja The Nasarawa State Government has called on health sector leaders across the country to translate commitments and policy decisions into measurable outcomes that will improve healthcare delivery, particularly at the grassroots. The Governor of the State, Abdullahi Sule, made the call on Monday while declaring open the Technical Session of the 67th National Council on Health (NCH) in Lafia, the state capital. This was contained in a statement signed by the Assistant Director of Information and Public Relations, Ministry of Health and Social Welfare, Ado Bako. Represented by the Deputy Governor, Dr. Emmanuel Akabe, Sule said the Council provided an important platform for stakeholders to develop practical solutions to the challenges confronting Nigeria’s health sector. He expressed confidence that deliberations under the theme, “From Commitments to Results: Delivering Quality and Equitable Healthcare for All Nigerians,” would produce actionable recommendations to strengthen the country’s healthcare system. The Governor described Nasarawa’s selection as host of the national meeting as a privilege and an opportunity to showcase the state’s peaceful environment, hospitality and economic potential. He also reaffirmed the state government’s commitment to supporting national health sector reforms and ensuring a successful meeting. He urged delegates to take advantage of the state’s hospitality during their stay. Earlier, the Nasarawa state Commissioner for Health, Dr. Gwamna Gaza, described the meeting as a historic opportunity for the state to host health sector leaders from across the country for the first time. He stressed that decisions reached at the Council would have far-reaching implications for the country’s health sector, urging participants to remain conscious of the fact that they were also beneficiaries of the policies and reforms being formulated for Nigerians. He also called for active participation and constructive contributions, assuring delegates that the state government and relevant institutions were available to address any challenges they might encounter during the meeting. Presenting the procedures for the Technical Session, the Permanent Secretary of the Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare and Chairman of the Technical Committee, Daju Kachollom, said the two-day meeting, scheduled for November 16 and 17, would provide the technical foundation for the main Council meeting on November 19 and 20. She explained that the main Council meeting would be chaired by the Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare, Prof. Muhammad Ali Pate. According to her, the Technical Committee would review proceedings and the implementation status of resolutions reached at the 66th Regular National Council on Health, consider memoranda submitted by the Federal Government, state governments and other ministries, and develop recommendations for consideration by the Council. item.title: Drug insecurity threatens national security, pharmacists warn FG
item.description: … Seeks 1% of seized drug trafficking assets to fund enforcement … Demands government control of medicine supply chain By Chioma Obinna The Pharmaceutical Society of Nigeria (PSN) on Monday warned that pharmaceutical insecurity poses a serious threat to Nigeria’s national security, urging the Federal Government to strengthen regulatory control of medicines and prevent the transfer of critical drug management responsibilities from public authorities to private interests. The society also called for the establishment of a special fund to tackle illicit financial flows in the healthcare sector, proposing that one per cent of assets seized from drug trafficking be dedicated to strengthening the enforcement activities of the Pharmacy Council of Nigeria (PCN) and the National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control (NAFDAC). The resolutions were contained in a communiqué issued at the end of the 99th Annual National Conference of the PSN, tagged IJELE 2026, held from November 2 to 7 at the International Convention Centre, Awka, Anambra State. The conference, which brought together pharmacists and other stakeholders in the pharmaceutical and healthcare sectors, was held under the theme, “One Health, One Pharmacy: Bridging Knowledge, Practice and Policy for National Impact.” In the communiqué signed by the President, Pharm. Ibrahim Tanko Ayuba, and National Secretary, Pharm. Gafar Madehin, the pharmacists maintained that medicines were not merely commercial commodities but matters of permanent regulatory control and national security. Citing Part I, Item 21 of the Second Schedule of the 1999 Constitution, the conference argued that the government’s responsibility for drug regulation and control could not be compromised by private-sector participation in the pharmaceutical supply chain. It cautioned against what it described as a private takeover of drug distribution responsibilities at the public-sector level, warning that such an arrangement could weaken inter-agency collaboration among the PCN, NAFDAC and the National Drug Law Enforcement Agency (NDLEA). The communiqué stated: “Conference reminded Government that drugs are a matter of permanent regulatory control and National Security, which is why it is listed as Part I item 21, in the 2nd Schedule of the 1999 Constitution.” It added that while government could engage private-sector expertise in financing and technology deployment, it should not surrender its regulatory standing or the cooperation currently extended by relevant agencies to Federal Central Medical Stores and Federal Health Institutions. The PSN further called for the integration of community pharmacies into Nigeria’s national security architecture and the Nigeria Health Insurance Authority’s proposed Pharmacy First initiative. item.title: 2027: Focus on issues, stop dancing at rallies, Pawpaw tells politicians
item.description: Nollywood actor Osita Iheme, popularly known as Pawpaw, has urged Nigerian politicians to stop turning campaign rallies into entertainment shows, insisting that Nigerians need competent leaders who can deliver good governance. Iheme made the call in a post on his Instagram page on Monday, where he criticised the practice of politicians dancing on stage during campaign rallies. He urged political office seekers to use campaign platforms to showcase their achievements, demonstrate their capacity to lead and explain their plans to Nigerians, rather than engaging in choreography to entertain supporters. The actor said Nigerians needed competence, good governance and purposeful leadership, not political hype and entertainment. “We don’t need choreography. We need competence. We don’t need hype men. We need good governance. We don’t need entertainers. We need leaders,” he wrote. He challenged politicians to tell Nigerians what they had achieved and what they intended to do if elected. “Show us what you have done. Tell Nigerians what you will do. You are not going for Grammy,” he said. Iheme also warned politicians against dancing on campaign stages, declaring: “I don’t want to see you guys’ dance on stage again. Be careful.” The post 2027: Focus on issues, stop dancing at rallies, Pawpaw tells politicians appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Actress Linda Osifo announces engagement after social media break
item.description: Nollywood actress Linda Osifo has announced her engagement to her partner, Mr Ose, expressing gratitude to God for what she described as an answered prayer. The actress made the announcement in a video shared on her Instagram page on Monday. Osifo has been off social media for months. In an accompanying post, she revealed that she had taken a break from social media before receiving what she described as a blessing she had once prayed for privately. “Not in my timing, not in the way I imagined, but in a way only He could have written,” she wrote. She said the experience was too beautiful to put into words, noting that some love stories were worth the patience and waiting. Reflecting on her relationship with her partner, the actress wrote, “Today, I look at the man God has blessed me with and all I can say is… God, You did this for me.” Osifo also expressed her commitment to her partner, saying, “To the man I get to call my forever, Mr Ose, I would choose you in every lifetime.” Announcing her acceptance of the marriage proposal, she declared, “I SAID YES TO FOREVER!” The actress further noted that when God authors a love story, every chapter is worth waiting for. The post Actress Linda Osifo announces engagement after social media break appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Germany thrash Netherlands to top Nations League group
item.description: Florian Wirtz scored twice and Brajan Gruda contributed a goal and two assists as Germany cruised to a 5-0 win over the Netherlands in Berlin to reach the Nations League quarter-finals on Monday. Derry Scherhant and Nico Schlotterbeck also got on the scoresheet as the Germans cut the visitors to shreds in the most impressive match of Jurgen Klopp’s six-game stint as coach. It was Germany’s biggest win over their neighbours since a 7-0 victory in 1959. “We hope that we can make it fun for the fans. It was definitely fun for us, especially in the second-half,” Wirtz told German broadcaster ARD. The Dutch defeat was the first since their coach Xavi Hernandez took charge but, despite Greece’s 1-0 win over Serbia on Monday, they also qualified for the final eight, although the last German goal dropped them to second in the group. The Netherlands offered little in attack after Germany’s second and missed injured captain Virgil van Dijk at the back, with the hosts cutting through a flimsy defence at will. So often criticised for a lack of end product since his big-money move to Liverpool in 2025, Wirtz has scored in four in his past four games for Germany. Germany knew only a victory would give them a realistic chance of reaching the quarters, with coach Klopp describing the match as a “final.” The game, a rematch of the 1974 World Cup final won by Germany in Munich, began with both sides risk averse and reluctant to move forward. The Dutch had the first good chance when Jurrien Timber found Crysencio Summerville unmarked on the penalty spot, but the winger lost his footing before getting a shot away. Just after the half hour, the Berlin-born-and-raised Scherhant latched onto a cross from Freiburg teammate Philipp Treu but hit the far post. Nine minutes later, Scherhant had another chance from the same blade of grass and this time curled a lovely effort across the face of goal and inside the post. The Germans continued their assault on the Dutch penalty area after the break, Wirtz adding another with a solo effort on the hour. The Liverpool winger dribbled from left to right and back centrally before lifting a shot in off the left post from the penalty arc. Schlotterbeck headed in from a Gruda free-kick with 65 minutes gone. The RB Leipzig winger laid on another goal six minutes later when he tore down the right and found Wirtz, who hammered in off the bottom of the crossbar. In his first Germany match on home soil, Gruda then added one of his own, tapping in a Scherhant shot which rebounded off the post. “We don’t mind who we play. We want to play attacking football. We want to score goals and dominate the opponent. And I think we did that perfectly,” said Wirtz. “We want to keep going next year. We want to get better. I think we’ve taken some great steps in our development as a team.” AFP The post Germany thrash Netherlands to top Nations League group appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: [VIDEO] 2027: Obi Won’t Get Up To Six Million Votes, Won’t Win Lagos — YPP’s Agada
item.description: The presidential candidate of the Young Peoples Party (YPP) for the 2027 general election, Peter Agada, has said that a former Anambra State governor, Peter Obi, will not secure up to 30 per cent of the six million votes he got in the 2023 presidential election. Agada stated this on Monday during an interview on Channels Television’s Politics Today . He said that the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) presidential candidate, who was of the Labour Party (LP) in 2023, won in Lagos due to the support received from different groups, including members of the #EndSARS group, youths, and workers. ﻿ He, however, said Obi would not win in Lagos in the forthcoming presidential election. While assessing the administration of President Bola Tinubu, Agada said that though he supports Tinubu’s removal of the fuel subsidy, he has a problem with the President not targeting the real end users and subsidising the product. He also said that Nigeria is losing about 70 per cent of its revenue to overbloated contracts. He also described the Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway ₦1trn budget as overbloated, saying that he would construct one kilometre of the road for ₦750 million or ₦800 million. Asked whether he was part of the proposed coalition to unseat President Tinubu, Agada said no one had approached him. item.title: 2027 Elections: ‘Nigerians Have Been Rejecting Him,’ Segun Sowunmi Faults Atiku’s Candidacy
item.description: A Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) chieftain, Segun Sowunmi, has criticised African Democratic Congress (ADC) presidential candidate Atiku Abubakar’s repeated bids for Nigeria’s presidency, claiming that Nigerians have consistently rejected his ambition at the polls. Sowunmi, who is also a member of the All Progressives Congress (APC) campaign council, made the remarks on Monday during an appearance on Channels Television’s Politics Today . Responding to a question about Atiku’s belief that he is better positioned than President Bola Tinubu to govern Nigeria, Sowunmi said the former vice president should reconsider his ambition. “Well, he’s been saying that for a while, and Nigerians have been rejecting him,” he said. FILES: Segun Sowunmi on Channels Television’s Politics Today “If you have done elections the number of times Waziri (Atiku) has done, there is something he himself must consider. At what point in time does he expect younger, sharper northern people to get tired or be fatigued at running around with him?” he asked. North Presidency Calculations The PDP chieftain, who was a spokesperson for the Atiku Abubakar Presidential Campaign Organisation in 2023, also questioned the former vice president’s political calculations, noting that the North had already produced a president who governed for eight years under former President Muhammadu Buhari. He further questioned Atiku’s candidacy under the African Democratic Congress (ADC), following a Federal High Court judgment nullifying the leadership of the caretaker committee led by former Senate President David Mark. The November 5 judgment, delivered by Justice Peter Lifu in Abuja, followed a suit filed by Nafiu Bala Gombe, a former deputy national chairman of the ADC, challenging the emergence of the Mark-led leadership. Atiku Abubakar is the presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress for the 2027 general elections. The ruling affected decisions taken by the committee, including the process that produced Atiku as the party’s 2027 presidential candidate. The ADC group has rejected the judgment and appealed. Sowunmi, however, maintained that Atiku’s candidacy remained uncertain. “As at today, he is not on the ballot. Because you appeal a case you lost in the lower court, does that mean you are going to win it? The bottom line is that, as at today, he is not their candidate,” he said. He also accused Atiku of mishandling the dispute involving Gombe, describing his approach as an “emir complex”. “Emirs don’t beg, emirs don’t visit people, call others. Emirs sit at home, and everybody comes to meet them. Yes, you can be an emir, but you can’t be an emir if you are looking for a ticket in another man’s party,” he added. item.title: US judge tosses new visa rules for Nigerians, other foreign students, journalists
item.description: A US federal judge on Monday struck down a Trump administration policy that would impose stricter limits on how long foreign students and journalists can study or work in the United States. District Judge Dennis Saylor, in his order dismissing the case, said the policy was “arbitrary, capricious, an abuse of discretion, and otherwise not in accordance with law.” The new visa regulations had been scheduled to take effect in September but were temporarily put on hold by Saylor, a move the Trump administration has already appealed to a higher court. The judge’s ruling stems from a lawsuit contesting the visa restrictions filed against the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) by a coalition of unions representing universities, teachers and journalists. In his order, Saylor focused mainly on the impact the new visa policy would have had on international students. “Put bluntly, DHS is seeking to prevent or discourage the very activity — providing educational opportunities for foreign students in the United States — that Congress sought to permit and encourage,” the judge said. He said the policy would “prohibit foreign students from engaging in extended periods of study, such as those required for Ph.D. programs; prohibit them from obtaining joint degrees (and) prohibit them from changing their academic concentration.” Under the proposed new rules, foreigners on student visas would be admitted for a maximum of up to four years after which they would have to apply for an extension. International students were previously allowed to remain for the duration of their studies. Foreign journalists would be limited to stays of just 240 days, or around eight months, but could apply for extensions of similar duration. Until now they could stay up to five years. Chinese journalists would get just 90 days, with extensions of 90 days. The visa restrictions are part of a broader immigration crackdown by President Donald Trump that includes aggressive deportation operations as well as new restrictions on legal pathways to citizenship. The United States welcomed more than 1.1 million international students in the 2023-24 academic year, more than any other country, according to official data. AFP The post US judge tosses new visa rules for Nigerians, other foreign students, journalists appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: [VIDEO] Bamayi: I’m Extremely Disappointed Security Agencies Allow That Joke To Go On — Sowunmi
item.description: A chieftain of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP), Segun Sowunmi, has condemned the recent ‘Bamayi’ protest in Abuja, expressing disappointment with security agencies over their handling of the incident. Sowunmi, who is also a member of the All Progressives Congress (APC) campaign council, made the remarks on Monday during an appearance on Channels Television’s Politics Today. He criticised the destruction of campaign posters and the use of violence by protesters who chanted ‘Bamayi’ at President Bola Tinubu’s motorcade, describing such actions as undemocratic. “I am disappointed, extremely disappointed that security is allowing that kind of joke to go on under the guise of people who are running democracy,” he said. Sowunmi argued that Nigerians dissatisfied with a political candidate or campaign should express their opposition through the ballot box rather than resorting to violence. “I expect people who have a point of view different from that of a campaign to wait until the day of election to exercise their franchise. But to be destroying people’s posters, to be carrying sticks and running up and down, that’s for barbarians, and I don’t expect any sane leader to do that,” he added. The ‘Bamayi’ chants, which translate to ‘we don’t want’ in Hausa, were heard on November 13 after President Tinubu attended Friday prayers at the Shehu Shagari Mosque in the Garki area of Abuja. Some protesters reportedly threw stones at the President’s convoy and destroyed APC campaign posters, prompting security operatives to intervene. item.title: Vanguard loses Online Editor, Femi Ajasa
item.description: The Management of Vanguard Media Limited announces with profound sorrow, the death of its Online Editor, Mr Olufemi Finayon Ajasa, who passed away on Sunday at the Lagos University Teaching Hospital (LUTH) after a brief illness. He was aged 44. A statement from the Editor, Mr Eze Anaba, said his death is a massive loss to the Vanguard family and the journalism profession. Mr Ajasa was a valued member of the Vanguard family, who made significant contributions to the growth of the company’s digital operations and online journalism. Born into the Ajasa family of Ajido, in Badagry Local Government Area of Lagos State, Olufemi Ajasa obtained a Bachelor of Science degree in Mass Communication, specialising in Journalism, from Lagos State University between 2004 and 2009. He further honed his professional skills with a certification in Advanced Writing and Reporting Skills from the School of Media and Communication, Pan-Atlantic University, in 2015. He began his journalism career as a photojournalist with National Mirror Newspaper in February 2012, where he worked until November 2013. He joined Vanguard Media Limited in December 2013 as an online reporter and content developer, serving until September 2016. He subsequently moved to TheNewsGuru.com, where he worked from 2016 to 2021, first as Online Editor and later as Team Lead and Head of Digital Operations. In December 2021, he joined Pulse as Editorial Quality Assurance Manager. Ajasa returned to Vanguard in June 2022 as Online Editor, a position he held until his death. His return marked the continuation of a relationship with the organisation that began early in his professional career. The management of Vanguard Media Limited deeply regrets this irreparable loss and extends its heartfelt condolences to his immediate family, friends, professional associates and all members of the Vanguard family. At this difficult time, our thoughts and prayers are with his family. We pray that God grants them the strength and fortitude to bear this painful loss, and that the soul of our departed colleague finds eternal rest. The Service of Songs/Wake-Keep in honour of the deceased will hold at 14 Sylvia Crescent, Anthony Village, Lagos, on Thursday, November 19, at 5 p.m. Other funeral arrangements will be announced by the family May his gentle soul rest in perfect peace. item.title: NNPP disowns Onu, threatens legal action over alleged impersonation
item.description: By James Ogunnaike, Abeokuta The New Nigeria People’s Party (NNPP) has disowned Prince Nweze Onu, who allegedly parades himself as the party’s Deputy National Chairman, describing him as an impostor who has no authority to speak or act on behalf of the party. The party also warned that Onu could face arrest over alleged impersonation, insisting that he had long been expelled from its fold alongside Senator Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso. The NNPP’s position was contained in a statement issued by its National Secretary, Comrade Oginni Olaposi Sunday, and made available to Vanguard in Abeokuta. He accused Onu of misrepresenting his political affiliation and attempting to create confusion about the party’s leadership. According to Oginni, Onu is not a recognised official of the NNPP and should not be regarded as its spokesperson or representative. “Prince Onu is not qualified to speak on behalf of our great party. He is, at the last count, a member of Kwankwasiya in NDC,” the National Secretary stated. Oginni further called on media organisations to exercise caution and verify the political affiliations and official positions of individuals before publishing statements attributed to them as representatives of political parties. “We are using this opportunity to call on all media houses to ensure that due diligence is done on verification of the status of individuals before publication,” he said. The party also condemned what it described as an attack on President Bola Ahmed Tinubu by Onu, dismissing his remarks as politically motivated and an attempt to attract attention from the Presidency. Oginni described Onu as an expired politician and rabble-rouser, arguing that his comments should not be taken seriously. “Onu is an expired politician and a rabble-rouser trying to get the attention of the Presidency. Nobody should take him seriously,” he said. The NNPP reiterated that Onu had no mandate to speak for the party, warning that individuals who falsely claim official positions within its leadership structure could face legal consequences. item.title: Lekki residents protest four-month power outage, demand substation
item.description: Accuse Eko Power, TCN of shifting blame; say businesses losing billions By Cynthia Alo Residents of more than 200 estates along the Orchid Road axis of Lekki, Lagos State, have staged a protest over prolonged electricity outages, accusing Eko Power Limited and the Transmission Company of Nigeria (TCN) of shifting blame for the persistent disruption. The residents, under the aegis of the Lekki Conservation Estates Community Development Association (LECECODA), demanded the immediate restoration of electricity supply, provision of individual prepaid meters and construction of a dedicated injection substation to serve the Orchid Road corridor. They also called for a technical audit of the Maroko 33kV feeder, through which the community receives electricity, and urged the Nigerian Electricity Regulatory Commission (NERC) to investigate the quality of service being delivered to the area. The protest, which took place at the weekend, followed what the residents described as five years of engagements and unfulfilled commitments by the electricity distribution company. It also came barely a week after the Minister of Power, Mr Joseph Tegbe, reportedly assured residents of Lekki and Ajah communities of improved electricity supply. The protesters, comprising landlords, tenants and business owners, carried placards with inscriptions such as: “Orchid Road Deserves a Substation”, “Orchid Road Band B = Band Nothing”, “We Pay Premium Rates But Get Zero Reliability”, “Eko Power Failed Promise” and “Constant Power Outages Are Killing Businesses on Orchid Road.” Addressing journalists during the protest, LECECODA President, Bode Akinwande, said the community had received virtually no electricity for more than four months despite continuing to receive electricity bills running into millions of naira. Akinwande described Orchid Road as a 7.5-kilometre corridor housing approximately 200 residential estates, alongside schools, restaurants, shopping malls, supermarkets, clubs, churches and mosques. He said the community’s size and contribution to Eko Power’s revenue made the absence of a dedicated injection substation particularly concerning. He said: “For the past four months, we have received virtually no supply. In the month of October, we did not receive two hours of supply cumulatively. And unfortunately, members of this community, various estates, have received bills in millions. And this is not acceptable to us at all. “For five years, the leadership of this community has engaged directly with Eko Power, and before it, the former management known as EKEDC. Several meetings have been held, and several commitments have been made. None of them have been implemented.” The LECECODA president said the current management of Eko Power also met with community stakeholders at Orchid Hotel and made further assurances, but residents had yet to witness any significant improvement. item.title: Jackson scores as Senegal move closer to 2027 AFCON
item.description: Premier League duo Nicolas Jackson and El Hadji Malick Diouf scored on Monday as Senegal beat Sudan 4-2 to virtually clinch a place at the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations tournament. Cameroon trounced Namibia 3-0 and Benin snatched a late 1-0 win over the Central African Republic to move close to qualification for the marquee African competition. Senegal, Cameroon and Benin have 10 points each from four matches and could all be confirmed as qualifiers on Tuesday depending on the other result in their groups. Cameroon and Senegal are former AFCON champions while the furthest Benin have progressed is the round of 16 at the 2025 tournament. Jackson came to Africa last week, having scored nine goals in all competitions for Aston Villa this season. He opened the scoring in a 4-1 home win over Sudan last Thursday. He also broke the deadlock with a fourth-minute goal away to Sudan, who hosted the match in South Sudan because of a civil war in their homeland. Defender Diouf, who moved from relegated West Ham United to Brentford during the close season, doubled the lead midway through the first half. Sudan staged a second-half comeback to draw level after 75 minutes through goals from substitute Al Gozoli Nooh and Salaheldin Adil. But a late Senegalese rally saw Pathe Mboup restore the lead, then set up Paul Mendy to score in added time. – Cameroon romp – Senegal won the final of previous edition of the AFCON 1-0 in extra time over hosts Morocco last February. But CAF declared Morocco champions because most of the Senegalese team temporarily left the field to protest a penalty, which Morocco missed when play resumed. Senegal have asked the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) in Switzerland to overturn the CAF ruling and a decision is expected this month. It took Cameroon 12 minutes to score away to Namibia through Mahamadou Nagida. Goals from Ryan Fosso and Saidou Alioum in the second half completed the victory. Benin left it late to secure maximum points with debutant Ede Oloko netting in added time. The goal condemned the Central African Republic to a fourth straight loss. Elsewhere, Zimbabwe outplayed Equatorial Guinea 3-0 in Harare, Guinea beat Eritrea 3-1 in Cairo and a Jordan Ayew penalty earned Ghana an unimpressive 1-0 win over Somalia in Essipong. In the six matches on Monday, Zimbabwe were the only host nation to actually play at home. Central African Republic, Eritrea and Namibia do not have international-standard stadiums. A civil war that erupted in April 2023 prevents Sudan from playing in Khartoum and Somalia cannot stage AFCON qualifiers due to security concerns in the Horn of Africa. item.title: Yobe Empowerment: Why Tinubu, Wali Deserve Electorate’s Votes
item.description: In a move aimed at fostering economic independence among vulnerable populations, the All Progressives Congress (APC) launched a zonal empowerment campaign on Sunday, distributing essential items to 500 youth and women in Yobe State. The initiative, which took place in Gadaka, Fika Local Government Area, saw the distribution of 200 motorcycles, 100 tricycles, and 100 sewing machines to beneficiaries, a gesture designed to create sustainable livelihoods and improve economic well-being across the state. APC gubernatorial candidate Baba Malam Wali, who oversaw the distribution exercise, emphasized that the program represents more than temporary relief and would be extended to the two other zones of the state. “Rather than offering only temporary relief, this initiative, which is one of thousands of lifelines created by Governor Mai Mala Buni, would have generational change impacts across Yobe communities,” Wali stated. Wali urged Yobe residents to cast their ballots for President Tinubu and all APC candidates in the upcoming elections to guarantee continued progress and prosperity. He cautioned voters against supporting opposition candidates, warning: “You can’t follow a road that is leading you to nowhere.” The APC candidate expressed confidence in securing victory through development-oriented policies and programmes, pledging to sustain and consolidate Governor Buni’s initiatives focusing on youth development, economic empowerment, and continuity. item.title: Budget 2027: FG moves to slash overhead costs, directs MDAs to share facilities
item.description: By Emma Ujah, Abuja Bureau Chief As the Federal Government prepares its 2027 budget, it is stepping up efforts to cut overhead expenditure by directing Ministries, Departments and Agencies (MDAs) to maximise the use of existing government-owned facilities instead of spending public funds on hotels and other privately owned venues for official meetings. The move is part of a broader cost-saving initiative by the Federal Ministry of Finance, through its Efficiency Office (E-Office), to eliminate avoidable expenditure, improve the utilisation of public assets and ensure value for money in government operations. According to Efe Ovuakporie, Head, Information and Public Relations Unit of the Federal Ministry of Finance, in a statement in Abuja on Monday evening, under the initiative, “The Office is working towards establishing a coordinated system that will enable MDAs to identify and access available meeting and conference facilities across government institutions, thereby reducing the need to hire commercial venues for official engagements.” She added, “A major component of the programme is the compilation of a comprehensive directory of meeting facilities owned by MDAs nationwide. The directory, which will be published on the Federal Ministry of Finance’s website upon completion, is expected to provide government institutions with information on available facilities and make it easier to locate suitable venues. “The arrangement will also enable MDAs with under-utilised conference facilities to generate revenue by making them available to other government institutions, while reducing pressure on government overhead budgets.” Ovuakporie said the initiative aligns with the Efficiency Office’s mandate to promote value for money, reduce overhead expenditure, monitor the utilisation of public assets and identify areas of waste across government institutions. In a related development, the Office recently inspected shared government facilities across the five South-Eastern states of Abia, Anambra, Ebonyi, Enugu and Imo, as part of efforts to identify underutilised public infrastructure and opportunities for cost savings. The inspection covered selected Federal Secretariats, Federal Polytechnics, Federal Medical Centres and Federal Universities. The exercise assessed the condition, availability, utilisation and maintenance of the facilities, with particular attention to areas where improved management could enhance productivity and reduce unnecessary government spending. Among the findings were under-utilised office spaces and facilities, deteriorating furniture, fittings and equipment, as well as inadequate maintenance of some offices and common areas. The inspection teams also identified opportunities to improve the utilisation of conference facilities and strengthen the organisation, storage and preservation of official records. item.title: Gunmen kill Operation Rainbow commander, one other in Plateau
item.description: By Golok Nanmwa Suspected gunmen have killed a newly graduated unit commander of the Plateau State-owned civilian security outfit, Operation Rainbow, and another person in an ambush in Bokkos Local Government Area of Plateau State. The victims were reportedly killed at about 3pm on Monday while returning from a condolence visit to Hurti village to their community in Tadai, Manguna District of Bokkos Local Government Area. The community leader, Machief Paul, who confirmed the incident to newsmen, said both victims were members of his community. He said, “They are all members of my community. They went to Hurti village for a condolence visit and were returning to Tadai when suspected gunmen ambushed and killed them. “They were killed in broad daylight this afternoon. It is very sad and unfortunate.” Paul disclosed that one of the deceased was a newly graduated commander of Operation Rainbow, adding that the killing had thrown the community into mourning. He said, “The commander had just graduated. We are deeply saddened by this incident, especially given the security challenges our people have continued to face.” Also confirming the incident, an award-winning Nigerian conflict reporter from Bokkos, Masara Kim, said the two men were killed in the ambush while returning from the condolence visit. The deceased Operation Rainbow commander was said to have recently completed a refresher training programme for unit commanders in Jos, Kim added. Efforts to obtain further details from security authorities were unsuccessful as of the time of filing this report. item.title: Oshiomhole tackles Atiku over education privatisation, says Nigeria cannot afford policy
item.description: …challenges Atiku, Obi to clarify education policies ahead of 2027 By Joseph Erunke, Abuja Former Edo State Governor Adams Oshiomhole has taken a swipe at former Vice President Atiku Abubakar over his advocacy for the privatisation of tertiary education, declaring that Nigeria cannot afford to surrender its public education system to private interests when millions of children are still denied access to schooling. Oshiomhole argued that privatising tertiary education would further deepen inequality and undermine access to learning in a country still battling a huge out-of-school population, inadequate educational infrastructure and unequal opportunities. The former governor spoke on Monday in Abuja at the unveiling of the Renewed Hope Education A+Z Scorecard by the Minister of Education, Dr Tunji Alausa. He questioned the rationale behind Atiku’s renewed push for private-sector control of tertiary education, recalling that the former Vice-President had pursued a privatisation agenda during his time in office. Oshiomhole also challenged Atiku and former Anambra State Governor Peter Obi to tell Nigerians whether they would sustain or dismantle the education policies introduced by the President Bola Tinubu administration if allowed to govern the country. He insisted that Nigerians deserved clarity on the opposition politicians’ education agenda, particularly on policies designed to expand access to tertiary education and provide financial assistance to students from disadvantaged backgrounds. Taking a further swipe at Atiku, Oshiomhole criticised what he described as the former Vice-President’s position on using public resources to enrich friends, warning that such an approach could undermine critical social investments, particularly education. He maintained that government resources were limited and that decisions on public spending must reflect national priorities rather than personal interests. “If the money he wishes to use to enrich his friends is not diverted to paying student grants, remember that resources are limited at any point in time. That is why economics is about priorities. What is given to those students will not be available to be used to assist friends,” he said. Nigeria’s education crisis remains a major national concern, with millions of children still excluded from formal schooling despite successive government interventions. A 2024 UNICEF estimate put the country’s out-of-school children population at 18.3 million, comprising 10.2 million primary school-age children and 8.1 million children of junior secondary school age, although the Federal Ministry of Education has more recently cited an estimate of about 15 million. Against this backdrop, the federal government has introduced several interventions aimed at expanding access, improving learning outcomes and equipping young Nigerians with employable skills.
